description: Zalatoris played in only four 2026 tournaments as injuries hampered his ability to compete at a high level

Zalatoris played in only four 2026 tournaments as injuries hampered his ability to compete at a high level
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:43 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Will Zalatoris will miss the entire 2027 PGA Tour season, the 30-year-old announced Wednesday. Speaking at the media day for the Austin Championship, a FedEx Cup Fall tournament, Zalatoris made it known that he will undergo spinal-fusion surgery in November to correct lingering back issues."I've been through four years of hell, so it's good to have something that will hopefully correct it," he explained. "It's not something you want to do, but when you have three tour physical therapists tell you it needs to be done at some time, you go ahead and do it."Zalatoris will play in the Austin Championship, scheduled for Nov. 12-15 at the Omni Barton Creek Resort, in what will be his first competitive start since the Texas Open in early April. He has played only four tournaments on the PGA Tour in 2026 after dealing with a torn labrum for much of the year.However, Zalatoris' absence has largely been due to a nagging back issue. The scheduled procedure will be his third major back surgery since 2023, when he had a microdiscectomy. Two years later, in 2025, Zalatoris required a disc replacement. 
"It's all connected together, and I just want to get it fixed," he said. "I can't promise anybody anything because of what I've been through. I'm the oldest 30-year-old you will ever meet."Starting his PGA Tour career in 2021, Zalatoris immediately jumped onto the scene by making waves at major championships. In his first 10 major starts as a professional, the wiry right-hander collected seven top-10 finishes, including runner-up results at the 2021 Masters, 2022 PGA Championship and 2022 U.S. Open.Zalatoris claimed his maiden PGA Tour victory in the 2022 postseason with a playoff win at the St. Jude Championship. It remains his lone victory on the circuit. The next week, he was forced to withdraw from the BMW Championship due to a back injury.
"I've been in contact with the Tour, which has been great," Zalatoris said. "It looks like I can come back in 2028 and play in the Challenger Series if everything works like it should."

title: NFL addresses safety concerns for Steelers-Saints game in France protests in Paris continues - CBS Sports
description: The league says it is still planning to play the game as originally scheduled
body:
The league says it is still planning to play the game as originally scheduled
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:48 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With protests on their third week in Paris and an NFL game scheduled to take place in the city in just 11 days, growing concern over fan and player safety has left some wondering if the league will alter any of its plans. But the NFL said on Wednesday that the game will go on as scheduled, with the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints meeting on Oct. 25 at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis, located just north of Paris."We're excited for the first-ever regular season game in Paris, and preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France on October 25," the NFL said in a statement, via ESPN. "As we do for every NFL game, including our international games, we work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We look forward to welcoming fans to Paris later this month."The social unrest stems from demands for the government to change multiple aspects of the education system. Protestors are asking the government to address under-resourced schools, poor conditions and teacher shortages. Students say the schools are falling apart and rats are in the buildings. The protests have sparked violence, with authorities using tear gas, stun grenades and various other means to attempt to stop the crowds. Protestors have reportedly set fires and caused damage. Police detained over 5,000 people in connection with protests, according to CBS News. 
Local officials say they are investigating both the protests and the police response. The French government is currently in a "political deadlock" as they approach the presidential elections in the spring. They have not responded to protestors with any plans or solutions for their complaints and demands. If the situation in Paris escalates, the NFL could reconsider its stance, but right now, it is sticking with its original plan. The NFL has changed game locations in the past due to extreme weather or field conditions. 
The Saints are considered the home team for the game, and their only listed event for the day in New Orleans is a private event where youth and amateur sports teams have the chance to play inside the stadium. It is scheduled for 8:30 a.m. local time, so if needed, the game could seemingly be played at Caesar's Superdome. But that seems unlikely at the moment.If the game does go on as planned, it will mark the first-ever NFL game played in France.  This will be the second straight year the Steelers play a game outside the United States, having played in Dublin last season against the Minnesota Vikings. The Saints last played an international game in 2022, visiting London to face the Vikings.

title: Burning questions for Week 7: Can Notre Dame pass first test, is Texas broken? - CBS Sports
description: A number of questions will finally be answered during the biggest weekend on the college football calendar to dat
body:
A number of questions will finally be answered during the biggest weekend on the college football calendar to date
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It is officially spooky season, but for college football fans we're living in seventh heaven. The week is absolutely loaded across the sport, and it affords us the opportunity to continue to learn about teams.That's what mid-October should be all about: getting to know why teams are real and which aren't. The junk filters out as conference play gets going, and the buy games are a thing of the past. It's an important part of the calendar as the ramp-up to the first College Football Playoff rankings truly begins. And it's punctuated by weeks like this. Outside of Ohio State vs. Indiana, perhaps there isn't truly a marquee matchup, but there are important things to be found across the schedule outside of that mammoth top-10 matchup. But this is also where a key part of the discourse is built for the playoff race itself. The SEC teams you thought were really good because they were highly ranked in September? Well, they're about to start beating up on one another the deeper into conference play we get (Florida, Ole Miss, LSU on notice there).
So what does one do with that information? The SEC would like you to do what benefits them. Look carefully at how the narrative begins, and you'll surely see the parity throughout the next few weeks. Because their losses matter but yours don't. And their parity below the best teams matters, while yours doesn't (mostly looking at you, Big Ten). Those questions will linger throughout the next few weeks. So what questions get answered across the nation in Week 7? 
        
            
                Loyal to a fault: These 5 teams are paying the price for sticking with familiar faces in 2026
                
                    John Talty                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Ohio State vs. IndianaHow far off last year's pace are the Hoosiers, really? This is not the Indiana of last season. They've yet to showcase a true penchant for tearing decent teams limb from limb like they have the last few seasons. They beat Ohio State last year in the Big Ten Championship Game, but they come into this one after surviving a road test against Nebraska.Indiana's defensive front is fearsome, and Ohio State's own issues running the ball are expected to be laid bare, but with No. 4 in Scarlet and Gray, Indiana's back seven risks being significantly exposed. Curt Cignetti called Jeremiah Smith a freak earlier this week. The game is at home, which should help the Hoosiers, but don't count on busts to bail out the Indiana passing game like the Cornhuskers so kindly gave IU last week. Can they stay efficient down-to-down, or will Josh Hoover's turnovers rear their ugly head?

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Florida vs. TexasWhat's really wrong with Texas' offense?  Arch Manning gets the headlines, and the issues typically fall at the quarterback's feet on offense, but there are more underlying concerns that are at the bedrock of Texas's offense. To get where the Longhorns want to go, they have to run the ball more efficiently than they are right now on early downs (first and second down). According to TruMedia, Texas ranks 110th in stuff percentages on running back runs among teams when filtering to FBS competition only.Overall, their numbers for stuff rate, EPA per rush, yards before contact, and yards after contact are simply woeful. They're 88th in rushing yards per game and 117th in yards per rush. They are simply stuck in the mud with a down-to-down drive efficiency rate because they can't run the ball, and it's giving the passing game no help. A lot of resources went into Texas' rushing attack this season, in the form of Hollywood Smothers and Raleek Brown.If Texas can run the ball better against the Gators, and they might, because Florida's defense has shown it is not up to the task in many ways this season, it could be the get-right game UT needs to quiet the noise, if only for a week.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Alabama vs. TennesseeHow much of a limiting factor is the Vols' QB situation? The uniforms will be neutral, but will Tennessee bring its offense to the party to match the sartorial success? The quarterback conundrum continues out of Knoxville, and it remains to be seen what George MacIntyre can do for the Vols if he's QB1. The early returns against a bad Arkansas team last week did not exactly leave much room for optimism. Bama went shot for shot with Georgia and came out on the wrong end of the scoreboard [Insert acknowledging the bad pass interference call]. How does Alabama put that behind them for the rivalry tilt?
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. Missouri vs. Ole MissDid the Rebels actually fix that defense in the bye week?Welcome back home, Austin Simmons. With plenty of players and coaches on the other sideline that Simmons is familiar with, how does the return home go for the former Rebel? He's downplaying it, of course, but it will always matter. One of the most important things about the matchup is how Ole Miss' defense stands up against Missouri. Simmons is fun as a passer, but Mizzou wants to do one thing first and foremost: pound the rock. With a zone run scheme that hasn't missed a beat in Ahmad Hardy's unfortunate absence, as the emergence of Jamal Roberts comes to the forefront, Florida tore apart the Rebels' run D. For Missouri's own tremendous run defense, how does it stand up to Ole Miss' rushing attack, which has Kewan Lacy back, theoretically much closer to full strength than he was last week?

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. UCLA vs. WisconsinDoes the QB injury matter? Nico Iamaleava is likely out for the season, and it's not clear exactly how much that will affect UCLA's offense. This is not a team that has been getting the job done with a particularly prolific passing game. In fact, only 12 teams in the country pass at a lower clip than the Bruins, and three of them are the service academies. What does Ty Dieffenbach have as the Bruins face a surprisingly good Wisconsin defense, which has found its form mainly by short-circuiting opponents' passing attacks?
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. Oklahoma State vs. HoustonIs the loser out of the Big 12 race? Don't let this game fly under the radar because this is a really cool Big 12 gut check. On paper, both teams are evenly matched. Both offenses are good. Both defenses are a little less so, but this is one of the two or three most important games in deciding the Big 12 race overall, as both of these two teams seem primed to take a spot in Arlington, Texas, if either BYU or Texas Tech falters. Oklahoma State does not play BYU, but gets Tech on Nov. 18. Houston lost to Tech, but doesn't play BYU either. The conference race will be crowded, and this will be one we point back to at season's end that helped decide it.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. Notre Dame vs. BYUWhat happens when the Irish are properly tested? Welcome to the party, Notre Dame. The Irish have seemingly taken the last five weeks off since their game against Wisconsin. If you'd forgotten about them, you would certainly be forgiven.
Heading into the season, it was clear Notre Dame's season would more or less boil down to two games: this one and Miami on Nov. 7. If they lose this game, their margin of error vaporizes, and the Miami game becomes a binary exercise for playoff inclusion, for all intents and purposes. Notre Dame found out the hard way what the downsides of a soft schedule are in their specific independent case and that one posed much tougher tests than this one did. BYU will be without its best player, LJ Martin, and, so far this season, has been missing a truly explosive element in the passing game. Playing Notre Dame when you're anything approaching one-dimensional is not a recipe for success.

title: No place like Rome: Mourinho gets UCL comeback win for Real Madrid and the last laugh - CBS Sports
description: The Portuguese boss faced off with his former employers and broke hearts with a wild comeback win
body:
The Portuguese boss faced off with his former employers and broke hearts with a wild comeback win
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:53 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        ROME -- There is no place like Rome, and if you're Jose Mourinho, it can get even better. It was an emotional night at the Stadio Olimpico as AS Roma welcomed Real Madrid and their former coach and lost 4-3 to the Spanish giants at the end of a crazy second half, when AS Roma were up 3-1 until the 83rd minute before conceding three goals in the last seven minutes with three corner kicks and the goals of Carlos Espi, Endrick and Toni Rudiger. Roma fans left the stadium softly chanting after losing their first match back at the Stadio Olimpico seven years after playing their last home game in the top European tournament. Mourinho, on the other hand, seemed particularly happy to win but was also received as a hero by his former fans. For the Portuguese coach, this is a statement win. He replaced players such as Vinicius Jr., Yan Diomande, Denzel Dumfries in the second half and won on his own terms. At the final whistle, he left the pitch pointing a finger at the sky: it was a crazy win, and it was also his night, defeating the club that he led to UEFA Conference League glory just over four years ago.
Gian Piero Gasperini, the current AS Roma coach, was basically the one who ended the stint of Mourinho at the Italian club, as the defeat against Atalanta that took place in January 2024 convinced American businessman and AS Roma owner Dan Friedkin to sack the Portuguese coach three years after shocking the world by appointing him. Two years later, the world is different in Rome. Gasperini is convincing week after week that he's the right coach in the right place but the defeat against Real Madrid is another signal that they shouldn't consider themselves at the level of the top European teams yet. With all the issues of Real Madrid that need to be taken into account, it was a moment of revelation for Gasperini and his team until the 83rd minute, before the mistakes of the Italian defense and the quality of the Real Madrid players took over. Until then, everything was just perfect: the performance and the players who scored the three AS Roma goals are a reflection of that. Marten De Roon, the Dutch midfielder that Gasperini had at Atalanta and brought to Rome this summer, opened the score, followed by Danyell Malen's brace, the most crucial signing that AS Roma made in recent years. But in the end, more than anything, it was mainly the night of Mourinho, as he made his comeback in the city for the first time since his sacking in 2024. A place that loved him like few before, and welcomed him with respect and admiration, the same feelings they showed to him when he was on the Roma bench were existent on Wednesday night.
In the first moments of the game, Mourinho didn't seek attention; he didn't need it. He spoke nicely about his former team before the game but he knew something would happen on Wednesday. All eyes were on him, even when he hadn't arrived to the bench. When the speaker announced the lineups, before naming the Real Madrid players, he welcomed "The Special One" who managed the club from 2021 to 2024, winning the UEFA Conference League, the first UEFA trophy in the history of the club, and losing the UEFA Europa League final one year later. 
The whole stadium applauded him and the AS Roma pre-match routine took place: the Champions League anthem, the emotional Roma anthem and then it was time for Mourinho again, a few minutes into the match. Roma's Curva Sud wrote on a banner, "Who brings glory to Rome, Rome honors forever. Your hands are blessed and the people tribute you eternal glory," followed by his name chanted by the whole Olimpico and more banners and pictures of him were shown afterwards by the fans. Mourinho sent kisses back, showing his love and appreciation to a place where he is more than a hero.It seemed a terrible night at one point when Roma were up 3-1, but the epic end of the match just made everything better for him in traditional Real Madrid fashion. 
He'll never admit it, but there must be a special satisfaction in beating the team and owners who sacked him two years earlier. He made a similar point about Chelsea and his former boss, Roman Abramovich, in a recent Netflix documentary. The bond between him and Roma fans runs deep, and their love for him seems eternal. In soccer, nothing lasts forever: results shape the fortunes of players and managers, and even the strongest relationships can fade with time. But Mourinho holds a special place in the hearts of Roma fans, and that affection will never fade, even after wins like these.

title: Shedeur Sanders trade rumors: Five potential landing spots for Browns QB - CBS Sports
description: Sanders' decision to hire an agent comes as Cleveland carries four healthy quarterbacks and speculation builds
body:
Sanders' decision to hire an agent comes as Cleveland carries four healthy quarterbacks and speculation builds
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With the NFL trade deadline coming up on Nov. 10, one of the most interesting names to watch in the trade rumor world is Shedeur Sanders. The Browns quarterback made a curious move this week, and it's one that could possibly signify that he might be on his way out of Cleveland. Sanders hired an agent on Wednesday, according to ESPN, after spending the first part of his career without one. Sanders has signed on with Adie von Gontard (CEO of Young Money APAA Sports), who also represents Sanders' former college teammate, Travis Hunter. The move was interesting for two big reasons: 1. As a player who was drafted in 2025, Sanders isn't allowed to start negotiating a new contract with his team until after the 2027 season, so it doesn't make a lot of sense for him hire an agent right now (If he's looking toward 2027, he could simply have waited until after the season to hire an agent). 2. The last notable player to hire an agent during the middle of the season was Marvin Harrison Jr. The former Cardinals receiver hired an agent for the first time on Oct. 9, and less than 24 hours later, Arizona leaked out news that he was being traded. By Oct. 11, the deal was done, and he was on his way to Houston. 
The only reason it would make sense to hire an agent now is if you need some representation heading into the trade deadline. If you have an agent, they can sniff around and see if you're drawing any interest on the trade market, and if so, they could then try to convince your team that both sides would be better off if you moved on. Why a trade might actually make senseThere's already been some speculation that the Browns are open to dealing a quarterback before the deadline. The team has four healthy quarterbacks in Sanders, Deshaun Watson, Dillon Gabriel and rookie Taylen Green. Through the first four weeks of the season, Gabriel was on injured reserve, so it made sense to keep all four quarterbacks. Watson served as the starter while Sanders served as the backup with Green being a developmental project. 
With Gabriel now healthy, there's no reason for the Browns to keep four quarterbacks, so it could certainly make a lot of sense to move on from either Sanders or Gabriel. Before the season started, there was some speculation that Sanders might ultimately end up as the starting QB in Cleveland if Watson played poorly to start the year, but instead, he's got the Browns off to a 3-2 start, and he has three fourth-quarter comebacks. This is now Watson's team, which makes Sanders expendable. Sanders did start seven games for the Browns last year, and new coach Todd Monken gave him a chance to win the job in training camp, but Watson ended up earning the starting spot. At this point, if another team shows any interest in Sanders, it wouldn't be surprising to see the Browns make a deal. 
Here are a few teams that could make sense as a possible landing spot: Buccaneers. Baker Mayfield is dealing with a thumb injury and that has left undrafted rookie quarterback Jalen Daniels as the starter in Tampa Bay. The Bucs don't have much experience behind him -- Easton Stick has been serving as his backup for the past two weeks -- so adding Sanders could certainly make some sense. Jaguars. This would reunite Sanders with his old buddy, Travis Hunter. The backup QB spot in Jacksonville seems pretty fluid. The Jags cut Nick Mullens in training camp before making a trade for Quinn Ewers in late August. If Liam Coen feels like Sanders is an upgrade from Ewers, the Jags could potentially show some interest. Broncos. A trade to the Broncos would send Shedeur back to Colorado, where he spent the final two years of his college career while playing for his dad, Deion Sanders. The Broncos obviously have Bo Nix, but things get a little dicey after that. Jarrett Stidham is the backup QB in Denver and the Broncos also have Sam Ehlinger, but Sean Payton might be willing to make a move for a new backup. Payton actually has a relationship with Shedeur and his family that dates back more than a decade. "I saw [Shedeur] when he was in junior high, and then I saw him in high school, and then I saw him when he was a sophomore in high school when they were on their way to Florida," Payton said before the 2024 NFL Draft. "He's going to, like there'll be this chip on his shoulder, and beware because this guy is going to play in this league."Cowboys. If you're making a list of landing spots for Shedeur Sanders, you might as well include the Cowboys. Deion Sanders spent five seasons in Dallas during his Hall of Fame career, and, given that fact alone, Jerry Jones might be intrigued by the idea of bringing in Shedeur as a possible backup to Dak Prescott. Dolphins (0-5). The Dolphins seem content to tank the season away, so they might not be interested in making a move, but if they want to add a quarterback to the roster, Sanders would be a solid choice. The Dolphins have Malik Willis as their starter and they have Kyle McCord behind him, so there's certainly some room on the roster for a player with starting experience like Sanders. No one knows for sure if Shedeur is going to be traded, but he's certainly someone you're going to want to keep an eye on between now and the trade deadline.

title: Agent's Take: Making sense of Eagles' salary cap manipulation after Lane Johnson's sudden retirement - CBS Sports
description: The Eagles kept Johnson on their 53-man roster after his abrupt Week 5 retirement. Here's a look at why and what
body:
The Eagles kept Johnson on their 53-man roster after his abrupt Week 5 retirement. Here's a look at why and what they gain from it
        
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:59 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    
            
    
        Philadelphia Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson abruptly retired due to personal reasons a couple of days after he was a surprise inactive for Week 4's contest against the Los Angeles Rams. The expectation was that the Eagles would put Johnson on the reserve/retired list because of his decision. Instead, the Eagles, who have suffered a rash of injuries, are reportedly going to keep Johnson on the 53-man roster. The roster decision is for salary cap reasons and also allows Johnson to change his mind about playing at some point this season, which seems unlikely. Johnson cited focusing on his mental health as a primary reason for his retirement in a statement he posted on his Instagram page.Johnson is making $23 million this year, consisting of a $1.3 million base salary and a $21.7 million option bonus. Half of the option bonus, or $10.85 million, has already been paid. The remaining $10.85 million is payable on December 1.Option bonuses are prorated on a team's salary cap over the life of a contract (including the option years and up to a maximum of five years) beginning in the league year when the option is exercised. This means Johnson's $21.7 million is prorated on Philadelphia's salary cap at $4.34 million annually from 2026 through 2030.
I suspect the Eagles wouldn't have hesitated to put Johnson on the retired list if the entire $23 million had been base salary. In that case, Johnson would be forfeiting roughly $17.9 million (14/18ths of $23 million), which would have come as salary cap relief for the Eagles in 2026.How NFL teams view retirementRetiring would typically put Johnson in breach of his contract, giving the Eagles the right to recoup money from him. Under the NFL collective bargaining agreement, an option bonus is only forfeitable if a breach occurs in the league year where the money is earned. Keeping Johnson on the 53-man roster means the Eagles won't be able to declare he is in breach and recover some of the 2026 option bonus. The Eagles don't have any recovery rights to Johnson's $18.79 million 2024 option bonus and $23.745 million 2025 option bonus because no breach occurred in either year.The recoupment standard is different for signing bonuses. A team has a right to recover the prorated amount of a signing bonus in the current and future years of a contract when a player retires. The $18.835 million signing bonus Johnson received in 2023 still has $3.767 million prorated in 2026 and 2027 for salary cap purposes.
Some NFL teams are reluctant to enforce these rights, especially for a player with a Hall of Fame-worthy career like Johnson. (Though that didn't stop the San Francisco 49ers from getting money back from Hall of Fame linebacker Patrick Willis when he prematurely retired in 2015 after eight NFL seasons, according to a conversation I had with a 49ers front office executive a few years ago.)If the Eagles processed Johnson's retirement in 2026 (when recoupment isn't pursued), they would have $42.89 million of 2027 dead money — a salary cap charge for a player no longer on a team's roster — from the bonus proration in Johnson's 2027 through 2030 contract years. Here's what the dead money would consist of:$3.767 million prorated from his $18.835 million signing bonus in 2023 relating to Johnson's 2027 contract year$7.516 million prorated from his $18.79 million option bonus in 2024 relating to his 2027 and 2028 contract years$14.247 million prorated from his $23.745 million option bonus in 2025 relating to his 2027 through 2029 contract years$17.36 million prorated from the $21.7 million option bonus relating to his 2027 through 2029 contract years, as well as a dummy/voiding 2030 contract yearThe $42.89 million would be $18.06 million more than Johnson's listed 2027 cap of $24.83 million. Johnson would be off Philadelphia's books beginning in 2028.
So what's the Eagles' plan? The plan is for the Eagles to delay processing Johnson's retirement until next June 2 at the earliest. That's because only the current year's bonus proration counts toward the salary cap with players released, traded or retiring after June 1. The prorated bonus in future contract years is delayed until the following league year, which typically begins in early to mid-March. By waiting so long to list Johnson as retired, this $42.89 million will be split into $16.614 million of dead money in 2027 and $26.276 million of dead money in 2028. That's likely what the Eagles were already planning for with Johnson previously stating 2026 would probably be his final season. In this scenario, Johnson's 2027 dead money is $8.216 million less than his current 2027 cap number.The $16.614 million will be the 2027 prorated amount from Johnson's 2023 signing bonus and his three option bonuses from 2024, 2025 and 2026. The $26.276 million will be the prorated amount from the three option bonuses in the next three years of Johnson's contract.
How Johnson's situation compares to othersTeams have delayed retirement processing before, but not quite to this extreme. For example, after Hall of Fame quarterback Drew Brees announced his retirement in March 2021, the New Orleans Saints kept him on the roster until June 11 because waiting was more advantageous from a salary cap standpoint.There is speculation that the Eagles and Johnson's camp will work out how much of the 2026 option bonus will be retained, given his roster status. It wouldn't be surprising if the $10.85 million Johnson is due in December isn't paid. The Saints and Derek Carr did something similar when the quarterback unexpectedly retired in May 2025 with an injured right shoulder. Carr kept the $10 million roster bonus for 2025 that he had already received. He forfeited the other $30 million he was scheduled to make in 2025, of which $28.745 million had been converted into a signing bonus for cap purposes. The Saints waived rights to $17.1 million of a 2023 signing bonus that was subject to recoupment due to his retirement.
For the Eagles, it remains to be seen how any potential savings from the 2026 option bonus would be treated under the salary cap. It's conceivable the savings would be applied proportionately. This would mean the 2026 through 2030 option bonus proration would be reduced by $2.17 million annually if the $10.85 million December payment isn't made. Under this scenario, there would be $34.21 million of 2027 dead money split into $14.444 million next year and $19.766 million in 2028.

title: While Man City defend their past, PSG show they own the present in UCL - CBS Sports
description: Enzo Maresca's tactical gamble backfired and Gianluigi Donnarumma struggled in goal, leaving Pep Guardiola to wat
body:
Enzo Maresca's tactical gamble backfired and Gianluigi Donnarumma struggled in goal, leaving Pep Guardiola to watch his former side stumble
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:12 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        There was an air of defiance about Manchester City, an arrogance that comes naturally to those who have developed a false sense of victimhood. Then again, they were not exactly wrong to boast some level of confidence – even if the Premier League found them guilty of 115 financial breaches, City had assembled a team that would at the very least contend in matches worth watching, even if the results could become invalidated in the not-too-distant future. City's supporters, Pep Guardiola included, filled Etihad Stadium on Wednesday with an expectation that the players on the pitch would not sour the mood, no matter that the guilty verdict suggests the collection of talent should not actually be there.Instead, what the stubborn onlookers got was a dose of reality.In some ways, it is not a surprise that back-to-back UEFA Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain would use Wednesday's game as another opportunity to assert their dominance with a 4-2 win. Their unique brand of dynamism is still a defining feature, one that is still hard to beat two years after manager Luis Enrique's tactical reinvention. Ousmane Dembele and Desire Doue are still impressively clinical, Vitinha still amongst the world's best in midfield. What was genuinely impressive, though, is that they were unflinching on a day that tested City's sporting construction.The hosts ultimately outshot PSG 27 to 15, racking up 2.5 expected goals while the European champions only tallied up 1.83. City's end product matched their efforts, Erling Haaland once again assuming cheat code mode with a brace that kept his side in the game while becoming the club's top goalscorer in the competition. Their defensive resolve failed the tests PSG posed time and time again on Wednesday, though, defined by a mistake-ridden performance from goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.The Italy international has always been a respectable option in goal but at 27 years old, he does not seem on pace to become one of his generation's top options. His inability to respond to Doue's opener in the 13th minute and Dembele's goal two minutes later was surprising, almost single-handedly digging his team into a hole they could barely dig themselves out of. It was a recurring theme over the course of 90 minutes, even as he saved Ferran Torres' tame penalty in the 90th minute.
Donnarumma was hardly the only person to blame for City's woes on Wednesday. Head coach Enzo Maresca opted to use Elliot Anderson as the lone player in midfield while just about everyone in front of him took a more advanced position, an imbalanced approach that was misguided from the start. It did not get the best out of anyone, PSG taking a 3-0 lead by halftime while City took just six shots and mustered 0.79 expected goals at that point.Maresca's halftime decision to bring on Ayyoub Bouaddi for Jeremy Doku and offer Anderson some assistance in midfield was to City's benefit but at that point, it was far too late. There was not much left to salvage despite a valiant effort, headlined by Haaland.Guardiola made a quick trip to Manchester to be a supportive figure but in the end, his shadow loomed large. The generous read of Maresca's tactical mistakes to start is that he borrowed Guardiola's famous overthinking habit for Wednesday's marquee matchup but in actuality, the new City boss does not have the reputation just yet to afford that kind of benefit of the doubt. Even then, Guardiola's ability to overthink was not the type of thing that would prevent someone from pointing out when he got something wrong and even if Maresca is the right successor, there is no reason to stop short of saying his choices were costly on Wednesday.
It was not the only way Guardiola's legacy hung over the Etihad, though. He receives a hero's welcome time and time again in that part of Manchester because he stewarded a superteam with his new position in the stands rather than on the pitch, the clearest sign as any that those days are a thing of the past. City's post-Guardiola rebuild means the team is still very much a work in progress, the team not favorites to win the biggest titles in front of them for the time being.It makes City fans' defiance all the more intriguing. While opposing fans expertly spent the prolonged international break successfully making Oasis puns to sell the point, a sign reading "What's the story? Tainted glory" at Anfield on Sunday, all City supporters could come up with was worship for club chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak. They have rallied around an executive and a series of businesspeople rather than the players on the pitch, all while erasing their actual case as victims – these are the very people who tarnished what should be the happiest sporting experiences, and ultimately what should be a storied chapter in the English game.The funniest part, though, is that for all of City's advantages, Guardiola's tenure looks more and more like magic in a bottle. Watching Donnarumma's slow response to Doue, another beneficiary of a nation-state's backing, it was hard not to ask: This is all City could come up with after all their efforts to work around the Premier League's financial systems?

title: Oregon rules Dante Moore 'out' against Nebraska as QB competition looms - CBS Sports
description: Dylan Raiola, who transferred in from Nebraska, and Brock Thomas will compete for the right to start against Nebr
body:
Dylan Raiola, who transferred in from Nebraska, and Brock Thomas will compete for the right to start against Nebraska in a must-win game for the Ducks
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:17 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Oregon listed star quarterback Dante Moore as "out" for Saturday's game against Nebraska in their first injury report of the week on Wednesday. The Ducks go into this weekend with their backs against the wall after suffering their second loss of the season against UCLA, dropping all the way out of the AP poll after starting the year No. 2.After a dismal offensive performance against the Bruins, Dan Lanning's Monday press conference was largely about potential changes on that side of the ball -- both in personnel and staff structure. Lanning admitted that "everything is being evaluated" after the loss to UCLA, but was adamant that he won't reveal anything the Ducks plan on doing differently before they take the field on Saturday against Nebraska. That includes a potential quarterback competition with Moore sidelined for the second straight game. Dylan Raiola, who led Oregon to a win at USC in Moore's place, had a catastrophic performance against UCLA, completing just 6 of 19 passes for 43 yards, throwing a pair of interceptions and losing a fumble. He was pulled in the second half for Brock Thomas, who threw for 149 yards and a touchdown to nearly lead the Ducks to a comeback, only to come up short of tying the game on a controversial two-point conversion attempt. 
Lanning has also opened up competitions along the offensive line and at some defensive spots as well. With regard to the quarterback situation specifically, Lanning did divulge some of his thought process on how they'll determine whether Raiola or Thomas will hit the field in the place of Moore.
        
            
                Once a national title favorite, Oregon has become college football's biggest disappointment
                
                    Austin Nivison                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
"[Saturday's performance] all plays into effect, and the body of work this week all plays into effect. The question was asked of me why not make the change sooner after the game; I think that's fair. On the same note, I think some of the positions we put [Raiola] in weren't successful opportunities as well," Lanning said. "I think we made some adjustments in getting the ball out a little quicker, creating some more open pictures that allowed Brock to do that. "But you have to be able to protect the ball, that's a part of it, and like I said after the game, Dylan's also a guy that played really well against USC and you have to be aware of that too."
Lanning knows this is a delicate situation, and he is understandably trying to protect Raiola because there is a world in which the Ducks need him under center and playing with confidence again at some point this season. That said, noting that the No. 1 job of the quarterback is to protect the football would seem to indicate Thomas has the advantage coming into this week of practice. On top of that, Lanning admitted there could be a change in who calls the plays on Saturday, but wouldn't reveal any plans beyond that the game-planning effort will be more collaborative. Lanning insisted he still has belief in embattled first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer and the rest of his staff, but made it sound like there's the potential for someone else to have the play sheet on Saturday -- he just won't reveal who. The play-caller decision can also play a role in the quarterback competition, as a more collaborative game plan will require everyone to be on the same page about which quarterback is taking the snaps and how they fit what they want to do. 
The additional layer of intrigue here is that Nebraska knows Raiola better than anyone, having had him as the Huskers' starter for the last two seasons. Given Lanning's desire to keep Nebraska challenged on who and what to prepare for, that could play a factor in which quarterback Oregon goes with on Saturday. At 3-2, Lanning seems to recognize that the season is one more loss away from completely unraveling for the Ducks. A three-loss Oregon isn't making it into the College Football Playoff, which means every week from here on out is a must-win situation for the Ducks.

description: Porziņģis also tried to quiet some of the online rumors that have circulated about his absence from the court

Porziņģis also tried to quiet some of the online rumors that have circulated about his absence from the court
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026

    5:58 pm ET

            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Golden State Warriors will begin the season without one of their expected key contributors as Kristaps Porzingis will remain sidelined indefinitely due to an unspecified health issue. Porziņģis, who signed a two-year, $40 million deal in the offseason, missed the entirety of training camp and all of their preseason games to this point, but returned to the Warriors facility for the first time this fall on Tuesday. Porziņģis and the Warriors each released statements on Wednesday offering a vague update on his status going forward. Porziņģis, 31, posted to social media that he's been working with doctors and is "getting better and better," but is still not ready to return to the court and must remain patient."Hello people, I'm working with doctors and experts to figure out how to be fully back to good health asap. Honestly, I'm getting better and better. I just have to stay patient, and I believe I'll be feeling great again soon," Porziņģis wrote. "It has definitely been frustrating dealing with some health stuff that you can't exactly pinpoint, on top of injuries throughout my career, so it has added up for sure, but we will get through it. Health is wealth. Thank you for all the support."He followed that up by speaking directly to the "internet doctors" who have been trying to diagnose him and tried to quiet some of the rumors about his condition. 
The Warriors said that Porziņģis met with general manager Mike Dunleavy and vice president of player health and performance Dr. Rick Celebrini upon his return to the team practice facility on Tuesday. The team did not provide a timeline for Porziņģis' potential return and said the "specific contents of that meeting will remain private.""Porziņģis will remain out indefinitely due to the same health-related matter but will be around the team," the Warriors said. "An update on his status, including the potential resumption of practice, playing status or timeline, will be provided when available and appropriate."
The Warriors added Porziņģis in a deal with the Atlanta Hawks ahead of last year's trade deadline. He played in 15 games for Golden State, averaging 16.1 points, 5.3 rebounds and 2.3 assists. The No. 4 pick in the 2015 NBA Draft, Porziņģis has dealt with health and injury issues throughout his career. While knee injuries were a common problem earlier in his career, various mysterious health issues have persisted in recent seasons. During his time with the Boston Celtics, Porziņģis was sidelined while experiencing fatigue and was later diagnosed with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS), which can cause rapid changes in heart rate, exhaustion and dizziness. 
Porziņģis was expected to take on a major role this season for the Warriors and being around the team seems like a step in the right direction. Still, until he's able to return, the Warriors' frontcourt rotation will be a bit thinner than initially planned. Al Horford and Charles Bassey are the other center options on the roster beyond Draymond Green, and the Warriors figure to play some small-ball lineups that could incorporate rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, who has impressed in the preseason, at the four spot.

body:
The league is being proactive in light of weather reports for Thursday's Game 3 in Cleveland, also moving up the NLCS by an hour
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:55 pm ET

                Getty Images
            
            

    
        The American League Championship Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and Cleveland Guardians shifts to Cleveland for Games 3-5 after the teams won one game apiece in Tampa Bay. Game 3 is set for Thursday and was originally scheduled to start at 6 p.m. ET, but MLB has announced that the game has been moved up to 1 p.m. ET due to "forecasted inclement weather" in the Cleveland area. "The change, which is based on forecasted rain on Thursday night in Cleveland, is being made proactively in order to remain on schedule in the ALCS," MLB said. A few hours later, Major League Baseball also decided to move up NLCS Game 4 between the Milwaukee Brewers and Los Angeles Dodgers. That game is being played in L.A.'s Dodger Stadium and was set for 9 p.m. ET. That's 8 p.m. in Milwaukee and 6 p.m. in Los Angeles, but it appears the league wanted that 8 p.m. ET time slot now without real fears of overlap from the ALCS.
The Cleveland area forecast as of Wednesday midday shows rain and scattered thunderstorms late at night and overnight. In glancing at hourly forecasts, it's possible a 6 p.m. ET start would allow the game to finish before any weather issues, but the league is being proactive to ensure the final few innings aren't affected by weather. It's a good move. No one ever wants to see the late innings interrupted and suspending a game until the next day is a major problem. 
        
            
                2026 MLB playoff bracket: Schedule, scores for Brewers vs. Dodgers and Rays vs. Guardians
                
                    Kate Feldman                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Looking ahead at the forecast, with Game 4 scheduled for Friday and Game 5 for Saturday, there could be further problems. On Friday, current forecasts around Cleveland call for rain throughout the day, though in the evening it is expected to be "light." At present, the game on Friday is scheduled for 6 p.m. ET. If there is an NLCS Game 5, it would be at 9 p.m. ET. Should the Brewers sweep the Dodgers, perhaps the league would move the ALCS game back. 
The Guardians took Game 1 of the ALCS in Tampa Bay before dropping Game 2 on Tuesday night. Gavin Williams will be on the mound for Cleveland and opposed by the Rays' Griffin Jax.

There are also markets here for which team/constructor car will win the event, which will have multiple cars involved.Here are the odds to win the United States Grand Prix, taking place on October 25, 2026. Odds are courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook and are current as of October 14, 2026.Max Verstappen +115Andrea Kimi Antonelli +230George Russell +1000Lewis Hamilton +1200Lando Norris +1200Placement/Top Finish oddsMotor sports betting offers users the ability to wager on drivers or teams having a certain placement or finishing within a certain range. For example, you can wager on drivers to place in the top 5 or top 10 of the event. You can do the same with teams/constructors.While it rarely occurs in racing, there's a possibility of multiple drivers tying for a position. In this case, there are  technically multiple winning bets. However, sportsbooks grade dead heats differently and the payouts can be different. If FanDuel declares a dead heat, half the stake is applied at the original odds and half the stake is lost. If there are more than two dead heats, the stakes are proportioned accordingly.Dual ForecastThis is where bettors can place a wager on which drivers will finish first and second. Both drivers must finish in the correct order for this wager to be paid out as a win. For example, you can wager on Max Verstappen and Lando Norris to finish first and second, respectively in a Dual Forecast market in F1 betting. However, if Verstappen finishes second and Norris finishes first, your bet will lose even though you did correctly pick the top two drivers for the race.Each Way BettingThis is not as common in motor sports but can be applied to racing betting. An each way bet basically places two wagers: a driver to win and to finish above another position. If the driver wins, both bets get paid out. The same applies for team bets in this market.Stage WinnerThis is prevalent in NASCAR and IndyCar, which has more laps than Formula One. You can bet on which driver or team will be in the lead after 25 laps, 50 laps, 100 laps and so on. These are the stages.Matchups/Head-to-HeadSportsbooks will put two drivers or two teams against each other, allowing bettors to choose which one will place higher. For teams, the bet is usually on the highest-placed driver for that particular team. This is one of the more popular F1 betting strategies. For example, if a market was being offered on F1 to see if Ferrari or Mercedes placed higher, the highest-placing Ferrari driver determines the result, even if both Mercedes drivers finish ahead of the second Ferrari driver. This means that bettors must consider both driver and car in situations like this.Group WinnerThis is offered in NASCAR. Sportsbooks will put a handful of drivers in groups and ask which will be the winner of the group.Top Car Make DriverThis is also specific to NASCAR, where you can bet on whether the winning driver will be in a particular car manufacturer, like Ford or Chevy. It's more applicable here since there are only two drivers on each F1 constructor, while car brands can span several NASCAR teams.Team of Race WinnerThis is similar to Outright Winner for drivers but applies to teams and constructors.Qualifying BetsBettors can wager on who will take pole position and which cars will be on pole. These are determined during qualifying racing, which typically takes place the day before the race. You can also bet on markets offering odds for who will finish in the top 5 or top 10 in qualifying, though these aren't necessarily  available for every race. The results of qualifying will often shift the race odds.Motor sports futures bettingFormula 1 bettingIn most cases, F1 futures usually apply to the next race. However, you can bet on season-long futures for F1 championship betting. The Drivers Championship is straightforward as it will be given to the driver who accumulates the most points over the season. The Constructors Championship takes into account the points for both team drivers. Only the top 10 finishers in each race score points, and those points are tallied over the season. The winning driver can be part of a constructors championship, but that's not always the case.NASCAR BettingNASCAR has different portions of the season. There are also different circuits like the Cup Series, the Xfinity Series and Truck Series. You can bet on marquee races for NASCAR in the futures market, and you can also wager on winners for these particular series.IndyCarThe major marquee futures market for IndyCar is the Indianapolis 500. Other than that race, there are season-long championship odds for the circuit.Can you parlay wagers in motor sports betting?While parlaying is generally not advised, as you don't get appropriate odds from sportsbooks that correspond to the actual chance of your bet winning, you are able to parlay outcomes in motor sports betting. While you can't pick multiple drivers to win an event in a parlay, you can pick multiple drivers to finish in the top 5 or top 10. You can also pick teams to finish in the top 5 or top 10.How to bet on motor sports live during a raceSportsbooks do offer live odds for motor sports, though this is likely a more prominent feature for NASCAR and IndyCar as opposed to F1. Driver and team odds will shift based on where they are in the grand scheme of the race. NASCAR and IndyCar allow for more leeway since there are more laps, while F1 can sometimes shift quickly towards one driver or team.Tips and strategies for how to bet on motor sportsDriver form does matter when it comes to racing, but the biggest predictor of success is usually how each team can adjust to conditions. Races can take place in all kinds of weather and team strategy can make or break the day. There are some teams that struggle to adjust, and bettors should know which teams those are before placing wagers. Historical track success often takes a back seat to current form. For example, Max Verstappen won the Canadian Grand Prix three years in a row and was a contender after starting second behind George Russell in 2025. Russell has had mixed results in Montreal historically but wound up winning the race after winning qualifying to take pole position.Longshots obviously don't usually win races, so they are better served as an inclusion in placement markets. You can usually back drivers who have had success on certain tracks or who have routinely finished just outside of a certain position market to break through eventually.Occasionally, a caution flag comes out when there's a crash on the track, which makes racing conditions hazardous for everyone. When this happens, there will be a safety car deployed, and all drivers must line up behind the safety car until the wreck is managed. There are different rules for each association and sometimes the race organizer makes a call in the moment, but usually, the race cannot end on a caution flag. If the wreck is too big to clear in a reasonable amount of time, the race will end despite the caution flag being signaled. Overtime doesn't really exist, but usually there will be at least one additional lap of racing should the fallout of the crash get removed in a timely manner and the safety car gets taken off the track.FAQCan you bet on motor sports?As long as you are of legal age in a state where sports betting is legitimate, you should be able to find a sportsbook which provides racing and motor sports odds.Who to bet on for the Indy 500?Because the Indy 500 typically takes place over Memorial Day weekend, you'll have to wait for a bit before placing wagers on who will win the signature event. Josef Newgarden won the Indy 500 in 2023 and 2024 but Alex Palou won in 2025 and is the reigning champion.Can you bet on SuperCross?SuperCross is a type of motorcycle racing. Some sportsbooks do offer SuperCross odds in certain states.Can you bet on motocross at DraftKings?DraftKings does provide SuperCross odds, which is a motocross competition, in select states. You must be of legal age and residing in those states to bet on motocross at DraftKings.How to bet on F1?All major sportsbooks have lines available for F1 races. Many of the same types of bets available for NASCAR races are available for F1 events.

title: NBA's most underrated players: An improving LaMelo Ball, a picked-on James Harden ... and a rookie? - CBS Sports
description: In wake of our NBA Top 100 list going live, CBS Sports writers are picking who they think are the most underrated
body:
In wake of our NBA Top 100 list going live, CBS Sports writers are picking who they think are the most underrated players in the league
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:57 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Every year, major media outlets (including us!) release a list of the best players in the NBA. And every year, that list is remembered for maybe a dozen or so slights. Social media typically rallies a handful of fanbases to outrage against how unfairly the outlet in question is treating their favorite player, and among those aggrieved cities, a few turn out to be completely correct when the season actually arrives, thereby invalidating the entire exercise in their eyes.In defense of those outlets (again… ours included!), the voting body is not a monolith. Just because one list is lower on your favorite player than you think it should be doesn't mean every individual voter was.And so, with our list of the top 100 players in the NBA now released, we've decided to give our voters the chance to join those social media hordes and explain where we believe our colleagues erred. Each of our voters selected one player, based on their own top 100 rankings and the final list we published as a group, to name as the league's most underrated player. Maybe we were too low on your favorite player as a whole, but maybe you'll cut us a bit of slack when you find out that he had at least one staunch defender in our ranks.
        
            
                Ranking the NBA's top 100 players: Victor Wembanyama enters 2026-27 season at No. 1
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Jalen Johnson, Hawks
Top 100 ranking: No. 30Why he should be higher: The Hawks' young star wing upped his production, improved his shooting efficiency and was the No. 1 option on a playoff team to earn his first All-Star and All-NBA selection in 2025. I think that's deserving of a bit more than the No. 30 spot in our rankings. Yes, Johnson showed some growing pains in the playoffs, but was also dealing with a hellacious Knicks wing defense that went on to win a title. It's not hard to see this guy continuing to climb the NBA ladder into superstardom this season, and at 25 he's got plenty of runway to continue improving. He will continue to get more comfortable with being in a leading role, and his playmaking ability at 6-foot-8 is what every front office dreams of.  -- Robby KallandLaMelo Ball, Timberwolves
Top 100 ranking: No. 41Why he should be higher: If you're a skeptic because of his defense, his durability, even his maturity, fine, I can acknowledge those are real issues. I don't think people grasp just what an incredible shot-creator LaMelo Ball was last year. From Dec. 6 on, the Hornets had the NBA's best offense last season. In that span, the Charlotte offense declined by 13.2 points per 100 possessions during the minutes played without Ball... just below the amount the Nuggets declined without Nikola Jokić (13.4) in that same window. Charlotte's starters had the highest offensive rating of any five-man lineup to play 200 minutes last year at a bonkers 134.9 points per 100 possessions. Well... let's look at how those starters fared without LaMelo last season. Brandon Miller's true shooting was four percentage points higher with Ball on the court than without him. The other three starters (Kon Knueppel, Miles Bridges and Moussa Diabaté) all saw their true shooting decline by at least eight percentage points without him. Last season saw Ball post his lowest individual scoring and assist numbers since his rookie year... yet it was far and away the best NBA season he's ever played. His presence is transformative for everyone else on the floor offensively, and keep in mind, he's mostly wasted that effect on bad teams. Now he gets to amplify Anthony Edwards, and I'm betting that will trigger an overdue wave of appreciation for one of the game's best young creators. -- Sam Quinn
James Harden, Cavaliers
Top 100 ranking: No. 47Why he should be higher: What are we doing here? Donovan Mitchell recently went too far when he tried to make the case that "the only reason" Harden isn't venerated like LeBron James and Kevin Durant is "because of championship convos." That particular caveat groans from the hilarious weight it carries. Mitchell went out on a limb, and it immediately snapped. But here we are at the other end of the spectrum with guys like Franz Wagner and Paolo Banchero ranked ahead of Harden. Harden is an 11-time All-Star with eight All-NBA nods to his credit. He's a former MVP. He's a three-time scoring champ. He was named to the NBA's 75th Anniversary team. Wagner and Banchero are ... not those things. Harden hasn't exactly covered himself in glory in the postseason, particularly where his defense and judgment have been suspect. Still, it ought to be possible to hold more than one thought at a time. He's surely flawed — just as he's better than we give him credit for in our rankings. -- John Gonzalez
        
            
                Top 50 NBA trade candidates for 2026-27 season: Anthony Davis, Zion Williamson and more names to watch
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Domantas Sabonis, Kings
Top 100 ranking: No. 68Why he should be higher: Sabonis missed nearly the entire 2025-26 season due to a knee injury. When he's healthy, Sabonis is one of the best floor-raisers in the NBA because of his rebounding, screening and passing. When the Kings had the best offense in the NBA during the 2022-23 season, it was because of Sabonis. He operated as the hub of the offense and created shots for others within the flow of the system. Sacramento's current system — and the lack of the right personnel around him — has led people to forget how good he can be. Sabonis, when healthy, is a top-40 player in the league. -- Cam SalernoCameron Boozer, Grizzlies
Top 100 ranking: No. 94Why he should be higher: It's strange to say a rookie is underrated before he's even played a regular-season game, and you can never read too much into preseason. But from what we've seen from Boozer so far, in addition to his college tape, it's hard to not be super excited. He already has NBA-level size and strength and is extremely polished on both ends of the floor. Just look at some of the stuff he's doing already as a 6-foot-10 forward. 
Plus, in Memphis, he'll be starting from opening night and given every opportunity to produce. All told, it's easy to understand why he's the favorite for Rookie of the Year in a loaded class. Whether he wins that award or not, there won't be 94 players better than Boozer this season. -- Jack Maloney
